text: @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers 是面向 DSH 的流程技能插件，通过技能 provider 将随包提供的开发工作流技能加入技能目录，并可在系统提示组装时注入引导内容。它提供头脑风暴与设计、分步计划、测试驱动开发、调试、代码评审和完成前验证等技能；默认启用 core 技能组，其他技能组可按需选择。普通 agent 会收到完整引导，子 agent 会收到简短工作者提示，用户也可按需关闭引导或指定技能目录。适合希望让 DSH 按一致步骤处理需求澄清、实现和验证的开发场景。代码未显示需要 API 密钥或外部服务。

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers adds development workflow skills to DSH, including brainstorming, planning, test-driven development, debugging, review, and verification. Core loads by default; optional bundles are available. It injects full guidance for regular agents and a short prompt for subagents.
想让 DSH 按步骤先澄清需求、再设计和规划开发任务。
能不能让代码修改先写测试，再实现并验证？
I want my coding assistant to follow a repeatable workflow from design and planning through implementation and verification.
@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers 的功能「技能目录」：注册 provider，按技能组发现技能文件并按需读取；默认提供 core 组。
@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers 的功能「提示引导」：在系统提示组装时为普通 agent 注入完整引导，为子 agent 注入简短提示；可关闭。

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Summary：Bring the obra/superpowers workflow kernel and its fused extensions into a DeepSeek Harness profile as one skill catalog plus a standing skill-first bootstrap. Use it when product sessions should move from intent through plan, test, debug, review, and verification in a repeatable order. It is opt-in and ships no harness peers.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Table of Contents：- [Summary](#summary)
- [Model Experience](#model-experience)
- [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work)
- [Dev Note](#dev-note)

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Package identity：Installable DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle that brings [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) into product sessions: a **35-skill** catalog split into core, advanced, product, and authoring bundles, adapted to dsh tooling, plus a SessionStart-equivalent bootstrap. The default profile loads the 19-skill core bundle (`diagnosing-superpowers` stays out until a deep dsh port).

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Package identity：Publish name: `@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers` (version tracks the harness family, currently `0.1.0-rc.41`). Source of record for this fork package: [github.com/oThTJx/dsh-superpowers](https://github.com/oThTJx/dsh-superpowers). This package is opt-in and is not part of the official main `dsh-base` composition.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · What it restores：| Superpowers behavior | dsh realization |
|---|---|
| Skills library under `skills/*/SKILL.md` | `ctx.skills` provider `superpowers` (packaged `skills/` directory, dsh-adapted) |
| SessionStart hook injecting `using-superpowers` | `system-prompt/assemble` section `skill:superpowers` with the same `<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>` framing (every non-subagent request); `using-superpowers` is user-only in the skill catalog |
| Platform `references/*-tools.md` | bundled `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md` appended inside that section |
| Subagent skip (`SUBAGENT-STOP`) | no full `using-superpowers` bootstrap when `session.header.origin === 'subagent'`; injects a short `skill:superpowers-worker` preamble instead |
| Model loads other skills on demand | existing `dsh-tool-skill` catalog + `skill` tool |

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · What it restores：The skill bodies ship as dsh-adapted prose under `skills/` (no vendored source, no git submodule). Foreign-harness tool names and platform references were rewritten for dsh, and the `superpowers:` skill-name prefix was removed. The published tarball includes `skills/`, `assets/NOTICE.md`, and the offline scorer `scripts/score-skill-first.mjs`. NOTICE records obra/superpowers (`2ce8aa15`, v7.0.1), mattpocock/skills (`5beb35b0`), addyosmani/agent-skills (`aeac41d4`), and bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD (`61e01f82`, with trademark notice) as review pins.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · What it restores：Capabilities that overlap are fused into **one** owning skill. When an upstream source has material that does not justify a second skill directory, it ships as a **reference pack** under the owner and is loaded only at the step that needs it. The catalog therefore stays at 35 skills while the fused behavior keeps growing.
@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Bundles：The package ships four bundles. `core` is always loaded; the others are opt-in through the `bundles` config.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Bundles：| Bundle | Default | Skills | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core` | yes | 19 | The day-to-day workflow: brainstorming, planning, execution, TDD, debugging, review, verification, finish, domain/design, security, sources, constraints |
| `advanced` | no | 6 | Subagent-driven execution and parallel dispatch, context engineering, prototype, wizard, grilling |
| `product` | no | 8 | Idea, PRFAQ, PRD, spec, UX, retrospective, course correction, and multi-role debate for multi-stakeholder product work |
| `authoring` | no | 2 | `writing-skills` and `dsh-harness-contributor` for skill and repository maintainers |

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Bundles：Core is always included, even when `bundles` names only an optional bundle. A bare install therefore sees 19 skills; a full install sees 35. The model-visible core catalog is 16 skills after `using-superpowers`, `handoff`, and `wait-what` stay user-only.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Matt skills and fused extensions：Superpowers remains the workflow kernel (`brainstorming` → `writing-plans` → TDD / debugging / review / verify). Selected [mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills), [addyosmani/agent-skills](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills), and [BMAD-METHOD](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD) practices ship as one fused catalog: every skill declares at most one `bundle` label, and that label is the only catalog metadata this provider publishes.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Matt skills and fused extensions：Session skills (`grilling`, `handoff`, `wait-what`) are absent from the model `<available_skills>` catalog and refused by the model `skill` tool. Users invoke them with a whitespace-bounded `/name` token in a user message (for example `/grilling`); `dsh-tool-skill` injects the skill body as instructions. `using-superpowers` is also `disable-model-invocation: true`, but its standing copy arrives through the system-prompt bootstrap rather than that gesture (users may still `/using-superpowers` to reload the body without the adapter).

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Matt skills and fused extensions：Obra skills that absorbed merges (keep on obra sync): `brainstorming` (inline Architectural grilling; Not Doing; Always/Ask/Never; reject aim-past-100), `using-superpowers` (≤5-line intent fork; anti-stack; tiny-edit; implementation priority; contextual gates), `test-driven-development`, `systematic-debugging`, `requesting-code-review` (Standards ∥ Spec + checklists + review lenses + doubt pass), `executing-plans` (slice discipline + impact map), `refactoring` (clarity + structural modes), `source-driven-development` (research mode), `codebase-design`, `writing-plans`, `handoff`, `verification-before-completion`.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Matt skills and fused extensions：Implementation and quality extensions: `executing-plans` owns the task loop, slice discipline, and impact map; `refactoring` owns clarity and structural modes; `source-driven-development` owns API-grounded work and the research mode; `requesting-code-review` owns post-hoc review and the in-flight doubt pass; `subagent-driven-development` owns per-task dispatch and parallel-dispatch reference. `dsh-harness-contributor` and `explaining-changes` live in the authoring and advanced bundles and do not enter the default core catalog.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Matt skills and fused extensions：`bundle` is catalog metadata only — not a router. Invocation frontmatter is parsed privately by this provider (plugin-only; upstream harness packages unchanged).

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Fusion map：Each skill owns one capability, and every selected source that covers that capability feeds its body. When two sources overlap, the package keeps **one** skill and merges both contributions — it never ships two peers for one job, and it does not drop a selected source's behaviour because another source moved first. Unselected capabilities are listed as out of scope in the debt table.

| `requesting-code-review` | obra Standards ∥ Spec · agent-skills quality body · BMAD review lenses · in-flight doubt pass | review request, lenses, a

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Fusion map：The map is an inventory, not a lock: a skill may gain a source, but it never splits into one peer per source, and a merged section is never replaced by whichever upstream moved last.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Reference packs：Reference packs are part of the owner's contract: `tests/superpowers.spec.ts` checks that each fusion pack listed above ships with its defining pins, that every reference file is linked from its owner's prose, and that every relative Markdown link under `skills/` resolves. A pack is not a second router and does not appear in `<available_skills>`.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Install into a dsh profile：Requires DeepSeek Harness peers (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill` and related packages), typically from the official CLI/`dsh-base` stack. Source-workspace `workspace:*` peers mean the matching DSH release; packed manifests substitute that exact version. DSH checks those peer ranges at install and profile startup and refuses an incompatible pair without an exact version exemption — see [Version compatibility](#version-compatibility).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers
```

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Install into a dsh profile：From a harness source tree:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers
```

Then boot `dsh --profile web` (or `pnpm dsh web`). If this fork's `dsh-base` already mounts `id: superpowers`, do not add the same row again — disable the base row first, or use a profile that does not include it.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Local / pre-publish check：```sh
pnpm run build:lib:host
pnpm --filter @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers pack
pnpm dsh plugin --profile superpowers-demo add ./firefly0621-dsh-superpowers-0.1.0-rc.41.tgz
```

(`pnpm pack` writes the tarball to the repository root by default. There is no per-package `build` script; host lib build produces `lib/`.)

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Enable from this monorepo without npm：This package is opt-in in the harness source tree. Mount the shipped overlay patch (or `dsh plugin add`):

```sh
pnpm dsh web --patch packages/skill/superpowers/cordis.patch.yml
pnpm dsh --profile headless --patch packages/skill/superpowers/cordis.patch.yml "task"
```

Fork trees that already mount `id: superpowers` in their base need no extra step; set `disabled: true` on that row to omit it.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Update Superpowers：There is no vendored submodule. To re-port newer upstream releases: for each source, diff **content baseline → target**, then walk every open row in **sync debt** below, then re-apply the dsh adaptation by hand. Do **not** use `assets/NOTICE.md` review pins as the sole diff baseline — those pins record last review, not “skills/ equals that tree”.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Update Superpowers：Adaptation rules: replace foreign-harness tool names and platform references, remove the `superpowers:` skill-name prefix, **keep the behavioral content verbatim** (dsh exceptions only in the table below), and distill Matt / agent-skills / BMAD ADDs (never dump BMAD `_bmad` runtime, memlog, HTML seals, or trademark personas).

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Update Superpowers：Since the v7.0.1 sync, `subagent-driven-development` and `writing-skills` keep their long guidance in `references/` and read a file from disk at the step that needs it, so a compacted session can reload one section instead of losing the whole body. Keep that layout when re-porting: a rule that lives inline again defeats it. The same sync removed the `executing-plans` worked example for the same reason, and rebuilt `brainstorming` onto the v7.0.1 text (which already carries `961a26d`): first message → conversation → playback → size the work, a design doc at every size (a short one for a small change), and a gate that never skips without consent. The dsh decision-support format for architectural clarifying stays inline and states its one-question exception; the older three-path router and its separate gate tables are gone so one gate is stated once. Every packaged `SKILL.md` stays under upstream's 20,000-byte compaction cut, and the package suite enforces it.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Update Superpowers：**Fusion, not port.** Several upstreams feed one skill, and each keeps its own role: obra supplies the behavioral spine, agent-skills supplies ADDs and OPTIMIZE merges, Matt supplies named extensions, BMAD supplies product-discovery distillations. Never replace a merged section with one upstream's version because that upstream moved — re-apply the merge onto the new spine and keep every selected source's contribution (for example `brainstorming` keeps Not Doing / Always·Ask·Never through the v7 rebuild, and `test-driven-development` keeps the agent-skills trigger breadth inside obra's description). When the contribution is a distinct capability rather than a replacement section, add a reference pack under the owner; do not create a second skill directory for it. Capabilities outside the selected scope are named as out of scope in the debt table rather than silently counted as ported.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Update Superpowers：| Exception | Why |
|---|---|
| Strip `superpowers:` / foreign skill-name prefixes | Catalog names are bare in dsh |
| Rewrite foreign harness tools → dsh (`subagent` / `subagent_fork`, `todo_write`, `dsh-tools.md`) | Platform adapter |
| `writing-plans` handoff label `Native` → `Inline` | Avoid “native harness” ambiguity; still means same-session `executing-plans` |
| `sdd-workspace`: refuse marker-less existing dirs (no adopt) | Deliberate ownership tighten vs obra; documented in the script header |
| Invoke bundled scripts via `bash …` | Packaged extractors may strip Unix exec bits |
| Keep catalog `Do not use` negatives / description contracts | Fusion routing gates |

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Version compatibility：This bundle declares `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages. DSH checks those ranges against the running runtime at install and profile startup; an incompatible pair is refused unless the profile grants an exact `package@version` × `dsh-version` exemption. Source-workspace `workspace:*` peers mean the matching DSH release; packed manifests substitute that exact version. See the [plugin manager's compatibility reference](../../boot/plugin-manager/README.md#version-compatibility-and-exemptions) for `version-exemptions`, `allow-version`, and the crash/data-loss risk.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · What the model sees：On every non-subagent request, `system-prompt/assemble` prepends section `skill:superpowers` whose text is `buildBootstrapPreamble(...)`: the framing below, the body of the packaged `using-superpowers` SKILL.md (frontmatter omitted), then `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md`. Agentless assemblies omit the section. `session.header.origin === 'subagent'` gets `skill:superpowers-worker` from `buildWorkerPreamble()` instead of the full bootstrap. Compaction cannot drop the guidance because it is reassembled with the system prompt each turn, not stored as a one-shot user message.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Standing order (before any tool call)：1. Call the dsh `skill` tool with the exact catalog name **before** clarifying, exploring, reading files, or acting — unless every tiny-edit condition in `using-superpowers` holds.
2. Anti-stack: load **one** process skill first; add supporting skills only when that skill delegates them or the user requires them. "Not an automatic workflow" means do not stack — not "skip `skill`".
3. Independent domains in one turn: issue multiple `subagent` / `subagent_fork` calls in the **same** assistant message.
4. After dispatch: finish only local work that does **not** need child results, then **end this turn**. Parent↔child talk uses adjacent `send_message` (Steer; tool returns delivery ack only — replies and `subagent-settled` arrive via inbox). Do **not** loop `list_agents` or status-ping `send_message` ("how is it going?") to wait.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Token effect：One large system-prompt section on every non-subagent request; skill catalog entries add their usual summary cost when `dsh-tool-skill` is mounted.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · KV Cache effect：Stable prefix for a given skills root and bootstrap toggle: the section text is loaded once at plugin apply and reused. Changing `skillsRoot` or disabling `bootstrap` changes the assembled prompt.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · What the model sees：Indirectly through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill`: every model-invocable Superpowers skill name/description in `<available_skills>`, and full bodies when loaded via `skill`.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Token effect：Scales with skill count and description caps owned by `dsh-tool-skill`. The packaged catalog is 35 skills; the default core catalog is 19, of which 16 are model-invocable. Optional bundles add 16 more skills, 15 model-invocable (`grilling` is user-only). Reference packs add no catalog entries.
@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · KV Cache effect：Same as the skill consumer: initial catalog after the reusable prefix; replacements append.

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- No runtime invariant companion is published; skills are immutable packaged files and bootstrap is a `system-prompt/assemble` listener with no independently observable durable event stream. Offline turn scoring lives in `scripts/score-skill-first.mjs` (first `tool/call` of each turn vs `skill`, plus same-turn `list_agents` counts after a `subagent` / `subagent_fork` dispatch); it does not enforce behavior at runtime.
- **No upstream hook binary** — bootstrap is a Cordis `system-prompt/assemble` listener, not `hooks/session-start`.
- **A complete persona replaces every section** — an agent whose composition registers a `complete` persona (agent presets) suppresses all prompt sections, including `skill:superpowers` and `skill:superpowers-worker`, for that agent.
- **Packaged preamble must avoid `{{...}}` prompt-variable syntax** — `loadBootstrapPreamble` rejects a complete `{{name}}` group at plugin apply (mirrors skill-always-apply); a custom `skillsRoot` that introduces one fails loud before the first turn.
- **Cross-harness reference content is removed** — foreign platform tool refs, Anthropic skill-authori

@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers README · Dev Note：The package owns skill discovery, bundle filtering, invocation metadata, and the system-prompt bootstrap. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`, `dsh-skill-filesystem`, and `dsh-tool-skill` remain upstream and unmodified.
